reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: lower tiled face / second roof course

answer.evidence: This is a 15x16 tile, probably a roof or awning kit piece. Row 0 is the outline. Rows 1-2 are a light band, row 3 is a mid-tone edge line, and row 4 is a dark eave shadow (L=50). Rows 5-15 form a 11-row body of horizontal courses with a second dark course line at row 12. The right strip (x>=11, L=66, rows 3-15) is a darker receding side face with a diagonal corner at the top right. The top band is short, but it has an edge line and shadow, so it counts as a top surface. The lower rows are ambiguous: they could be more roof courses or a front face. Either way there is a 3+ row face under the top band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block of about 24x28 px at 2x, roughly one tile. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It has 6 visible tones per tile against 10-12 for the references, and only about 3 lightness steps across a few horizontal bands. Its outline is a tinted dark purple (0% neutral dark edge), so it is not near-black. It has no tile scallops, plaster speckle, stone-by-stone shading or grain. The references carry a full tiled roof with per-tile highlights, timber framing, speckled plaster and individually shaded stones. Next to them the candidate looks thin and simple, like a small sticker-like prop rather than a building. Fail.

answer.evidence: The cell is a single repeating roof or awning tile pattern. Light courses sit at rows 1-2, 9-11 and 13-15, with dark separator lines at rows 4 and 12. The silhouette is 15 px wide from row 3 down and has a clipped top-right corner. The dark right-hand columns (x about 11-14, L=66) read as a receding side face. No vertical south face is drawn, because the bottom rows 13-15 repeat the same light tile color as rows 9-11. So the whole cell is a roof plane with no front wall, which makes it a flat slab, probably a roof piece meant to sit above a separate wall cell.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple-blue block about 24x28 px at 2x, with no visible roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not read as a whole building like the references. It uses 6 visible tones in total, against 10-12 per tile for the references. It shows only 2-3 lightness steps, in a few horizontal bands with a dark edge. The references have 5-6 steps per material, with per-tile roof highlights, plaster speckle and stone shading. Texture is minimal: no scallops, grain or clumps. The outline is a dark tinted purple, not a neutral black line, but it is too thin to judge as a material-tone outline. The piece is far smaller and simpler than the references, and density is much lower by eye.

surfaces.part: roof/awning plane drawn as horizontal tile or stripe courses (corner piece of a kit)

answer.evidence: The 15-16 px cell is filled with repeating horizontal stripe courses: light rows 1-2, mid row 3, dark line row 4, mid rows 5-8, light rows 9-11, dark line row 12, light rows 13-15. Together they read as one continuous roof or awning plane. The dark lines at rows 4 and 12 are course shadows between stripes, not an eave above a separate wall. No distinct vertical south face of 3 or more rows sits below a front-edge line; the bottom light band rows 13-15 continues the same stripe pattern. A 4 px dark strip at the right (x=11-14, rows 3-15) with a gray diagonal corner at the top right is a receding side or corner piece. So there is a roof surface and a side strip, but no real front elevation, and I read it as a slab-like roof tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block of about 16x16 px (a crate or shelf), not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It has 6 visible tones per tile against 10-12 in the references, so it is much lower in density. It shows only about 3 lightness steps on its main ramp, with a few horizontal stripes, and no tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. Its edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline reads as a dark purple material tone, not near-black. Near-flat coverage is 0%, but that is only because the piece is so small. Next to the roofed, textured references it looks far thinner and simpler.

surfaces.part: mid horizontal stripe band (repeats the band, edge line and shadow pattern)

answer.evidence: The silhouette grows from 12 to 15 px wide over rows 0-3, then stays at 15 px to row 15. The only top-like part is the light band at rows 1-2, with an edge line at row 3 and a dark shadow row at 4. That is a 2-row rim or cornice, too thin to read as a top surface. Below it, rows 5-15 are a vertical face of repeating horizontal stripes. The light stripe at rows 9-11 with its edge line and dark row 12 is another flat stripe on the face, not a horizontal surface. Columns x=11 and up are a uniform dark strip (L=66) from row 3 down, which reads as a shaded side or edge. The whole piece reads as a front-facing wall or awning panel with no real top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple block, about one tile in size, and it does not read as a whole building. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It shows about 3 visible lightness steps (light top, mid body, dark base) against about 6 on the reference roofs. The measured facts give 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references. The 0% near-flat figure comes from the small horizontal slat lines, but there is no scalloped tile texture, speckle or per-element shading as on the references. The 0% neutral share on dark edge pixels means the outline is tinted, but with only 6 colours in total the shading is shallow and sticker-like. The references have 66 to 185 distinct colours with grain and tile highlights. The candidate is far thinner and flatter than either, so it fails.
